subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- September 24, 2026
body:
geocode-glib conflict resolved in acreetionos + acreetionos-xlibre  

The merge of the release‑1 branch into main finally cleared the geocode‑glib update clash that had plagued both the main and Xlibre builds for weeks, letting users on the latest ISO finally get functional geolocation services again. Darren (@cobra3282000) and Natalie (@spivanatalie64) rolled out the fix as part of a coordinated push that also restored firefox‑ublock-origin to the Xlibre pipeline, ensuring privacy tools stay in place.  

Development  
The fix landed in AcreetionOS‑Xlibre after a careful cherry‑pick from release‑1, smoothing the transition for anyone who upgrades via the flash utility. The CI job now also passes the `-R` flag to `gh release create`, which eliminates the extra checkout step and speeds up ISO publishing for future releases. All changes are logged on the changelog page, so you can see exactly what shifted.  

Community  
Systemd v262 hit the streets with a single‑binary static build option and improved kernel coredump support, giving anyone who upgrades a snappier init system. Meanwhile, a critical vulnerability in the Radicle peer‑to‑peer protocol was disclosed, urging users to patch and stay aware of the security landscape. The discord server at https://discord.acreetionos.org is buzzing with thanks for the quick resolution.  

Tip of the day  
Check out the wiki at https://acreetionos.org/wiki.html for a step‑by‑step guide on using the flash utility to install the newest ISO, and make sure you have firefox‑ublock-origin enabled for extra privacy.  

For the latest updates and downloads, head to the homepage https://acreetionos.org/.
